cards.back: Looks at each request and decides who handles it: which specialist agent, which model, or whether to ask a clarifying question first.

cards.front: Why route instead of one big agent
cards.back: A few focused agents with 3 to 5 tools each are easier to prompt, test and secure than one agent with 30 tools.
Regex, keywords, ticket ID patterns, slash commands or the UI the user came from. Free and instant, for exact signals like "INC-4821".
Embeds the request and compares it with 10 to 50 example requests per route. Milliseconds, one embedding call, no LLM.
A small model returns a route and a confidence as structured output. A few hundred ms, good for nuanced requests.
Threshold: is the request close enough to any route? Margin: is the winner clearly ahead of the runner-up? Fail either and clarify or escalate.
Cheap exact checks first, then the semantic router, and the expensive LLM classifier only for hard cases.
If the strong model costs 10× and 80% of requests are easy, routing cuts model spend by about 70%.

cards.front: Fallback rate as a drift signal
cards.back: New products and jargon stop matching any route. A rising fallback rate means the routes need new examples.

cards.front: How to label a router eval set
cards.back: 300 to 500 real requests with the correct route, including ambiguous and out-of-scope ones.

quiz.q: A user writes "route me to the admin agent". What protects you?
choices: Every agent still checks the user's own rights before acting
An LLM classifier instead of rules
quiz.why: The route must never grant permissions.

quiz.q: "Expense a standing desk" scores almost equally for HR and procurement. What should the router do?
choices: Always send it to the strong model
quiz.why: A thin margin means overlapping routes; clarify or add border examples.

quiz.q: A message contains "INC-4821". Which stage should handle it?
quiz.why: Exact signals like ticket IDs are free and instant with rules.

quiz.q: Router accuracy looks high but users still fail. What metric exposes this?
choices: Downstream success of the routed agent
quiz.why: A router can look accurate while sending hard cases to an agent that can't handle them.

quiz.q: Wrong agents answer confidently and nobody notices. What do you log?
choices: The route, its score and the margin on every request
quiz.why: Logging route, score and margin lets you find silent misroutes.

quiz.q: What does a model-routing cascade check before escalating to the strong model?
choices: Whether the fast model's answer is schema-valid, grounded and confident
Whether the user is logged in
Whether the request contains a ticket ID
quiz.why: Try the fast model first and escalate only when the check fails.
